claim: PonderTTT gates test-time-training updates per input using the TTT layer's self-supervised reconstruction loss as a training-free confidence signal, rather than applying uniform compute to all inputs.
scope_conditions: GPT-2 models 124M-1.5B, code language modeling on The Stack v2, teacher-forced perplexity, not discrete coding-problem solving
quoted_support: Our Reconstruction Gating achieves 82-89% Oracle Recovery while being fully training-free, significantly outperforming Random Skip baselines (up to 16% lower loss on OOD languages).
numbers: up to 16% lower loss on OOD languages

claim: The adaptive-compute-allocation signal used by PonderTTT is inference-compatible and requires no ground-truth labels, only a self-calibrated scalar threshold adapted via EMA.
quoted_support: The gating decision itself is training-free--requiring no learned classifier or auxiliary networks; only a single scalar threshold is initially calibrated on unlabeled data and continuously adapted via EMA to maintain target update rates.

claim: Existing adaptive test-time-compute work for code applies at the granularity of the whole input sequence (per-token or per-document reconstruction loss), not at the granularity of individual behavioral requirements within a single coding problem.
stance_target: novelty of per-requirement test-time compute allocation (candidate b)
scope_conditions: code language modeling literature as of July 2026
quoted_support: Large language models apply uniform computation to all inputs, regardless of difficulty.
